findings.description: [qodo] valid_actual_range only checks that actual line_range is a two-element sequence of ints (not bools); it does not enforce a 1-based, non-empty range (start >= 1 and start <= end). A malformed actual range such as [0, 5] is accepted and can overlap an expected 1-based range, producing a false hit. Since state.json is arbitrary input, malformed ranges should be treated as absent per the docstring.

[qodo] file and description validation passes whitespace-only strings because it checks `not file` / `not description` rather than stripping. A whitespace-only file or description can never match findings and silently poisons the answer key.

[expert] valid_actual_range checks only type, arity, and intness. Semantically invalid ranges such as [0, 999999] or [5, 1] are treated as valid, so the documented description fallback for malformed actual ranges is skipped and scoring can be wrong.

[expert] _read_confirmed_findings repeats the shape-only line_range validation and does not check start >= 1 or end >= start. Malformed CONFIRMED ranges flow into finding_hit as valid, so scoring depends on duplicated validation that can drift.

[expert] _score_findings/_pick_best_findings are scoring policy but live in runner.py. This splits findings-scoring responsibility between runner and scorer (finding_hit) and weakens module cohesion; move them next to finding_hit in scorer.py.

[expert] Description fallback requires at least two significant tokens. The corpus parser accepts any non-empty description, so an expected_findings entry whose description contains fewer than two tokens of length >=4 can never hit and silently becomes a miss. Validate token count at parse time or define a fallback.

[adversarial] finding_hit only checks that actual line_range is a two-int list/tuple; it does not enforce start >= 1 or start <= end. A malformed actual range such as [0, 100] can overlap an expected range and score a false hit, even though the docstring says malformed actual ranges are treated as absent.

[adversarial] _read_confirmed_findings passes through any two-int list as a valid line_range without validating order or positivity. This means state.json with [5, 1] or [0, 100] reaches finding_hit as valid and can cause false overlap hits/misses.

[adversarial] _score_findings counts hits independently for each expected finding, so one actual finding that overlaps multiple expected findings (duplicated answer entries or overlapping descriptions/ranges) is counted as multiple hits. This can inflate finding_hits.
